title: Failure Explorer: unified error analysis workflow for Console
creator: Sofia Lin
description: Design and prototype a consolidated 'Failure Explorer' panel in Redwood Console that lets engineers and SREs triage failed requests across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The goal is to surface error taxonomy, retry patterns, request payload inspection (sanitized), and quick remediation actions (retry, rollback route, open incident). The panel should integrate with rollouts and cost dashboards so users can correlate failures with recent model/route changes.
notes: Primary UX goals: fast triage, clear root-cause signals, minimal context switching.
We intentionally avoid a full trace playback initially to reduce engineering scope; instead provide a dense timeline + payload inspector that supports step-through of retry attempts.

Privacy/trust trade-off: full request/response payloads should be opt-in and masked by default for hosted customers; for Private deployments, expose a configuration toggle. This needs a security review (see security_review_required).

Performance trade-off: fetching raw payloads for many events can be expensive. Implement lazy-loading and size caps; include a warning when payloads exceed 2MB and provide a download link instead of inline rendering.
Accessibility: ensure the timeline and taxonomy lists are keyboard navigable and work with screen readers; color choices must not be the sole means of conveying severity.
Design decision: use a right-side flyout inspector for payloads on small screens, and a persistent inspector column on wide screens to support comparison between attempts.

Rollout integration: show a sticky banner when viewing failures that were introduced in a recent rollout (link to rollout details) and allow one-click rollback or pin older model variants for debugging.
Metric correlation: surface token-level latency and cost delta for failed vs successful requests in the same time window.
Prototype links and PRs are below; next step is engineering estimation and security review scheduling.
